text:
may: Quick report from the onboarding quickstart stress run: when we force token rotations the sample app produced a concentrated retry burst and a few duplicate resource creations (non-idempotent).

kai: Can you paste the minimal timeline/logs? wondering if it's SDK behavior or an outer proxy.

may: Short timeline from the harness:
```
2026-08-12T16:45:00Z request id=tx42 auth=Bearer tok_old -> 401
2026-08-12T16:45:00Z onAuthRefresh started
2026-08-12T16:45:00Z onAuthRefresh done -> tok_new
2026-08-12T16:45:00Z SDK retried tx42 immediately (no jitter) -> upstream 429
2026-08-12T16:45:00Z SDK backoff counter reset -> retried quickly again -> duplicate created
```

olivia: Yikes. That pattern (resetting backoff when onAuthRefresh resolves) rings a bellwe saw a parity gap in an old audit where JS reset and Py preserved. If many clients refresh in lockstep you can amplify a retry storm.

sam: Confirmed: the lightweight onboarding wrapper (JS) currently reconstructs the RetryState after a refresh which zeros attempt_count. The proper behavior is to preserve attempt_count and next_delay so a refresh doesn't accelerate retries.

kai: Short-term mitigation plan proposed:
- Preserve retry state across onAuthRefresh resolution in the JS SDK (parity with Py/Go).
- Add small randomized jitter before the immediate post-refresh retry (suggest uniform 30-180ms) to desynchronize clients.
- Update sample app to attach an Idempotency-Key header for create operations and document the recommendation in the quickstart README.
- Add a tiny CI harness test that simulates 80 parallel clients rotating tokens and asserts duplicate creations <1%.

may: I like that. One nuance: some onboarding flows intentionally have side-effects that are safe to dedupe only server-side. Recommend we also land a short server doc for handlers to honor Idempotency-Key when present.

olivia: Also, add diagnostics in the sample harness logs showing retry_state (attempt_count/next_delay) on each retry to make postmortems easier.

sam: Implementation notes for JS SDK fix:
- Keep existing RetryState object, thread-local to a logical request, and do not reconstruct it on auth refresh resolution.
- Where we currently call `resetRetry()` in the auth-success path, replace with `resumeRetry()` preserving attempt count.
- Add a unit test that fakes auth refresh and asserts attempt_count and nextDelay unchanged.
- Add an integration test in the sample-onboard repo that runs with TTL=3s and 100 clients for 30s, recording duplicate counts.

kai: infra-bot: schedule CI runs and staging deploys for the patches.

infra-bot: CI job queued: branch "devex/fix-preserve-retry-state" will run unit + integ in staging at 2026-08-13T02:00Z.

may: I've filed INFR-9402 with logs, the repro harness, and the suggested patch list (preserve retry state, post-refresh jitter, idempotency header in sample app). Marking P2. Link: https://redwood-internal/issues/INFR-9402

olivia: I'll add the jitter wrapper as a small, opt-out flag in the JS SDK so we can tune the range quickly if staging shows issues.

sam: After staging deploy, let's run a 100-client overnight run and compare duplicate counts to baseline. If duplicates persist above 0.5%, we consider adding server-side best-effort throttling for onboarding endpoints.

kai: Agreed. Also add a small telemetry ping when a token refresh happens within 1s of a retry and we get a 429; helps measure prevalence across customers. Keep it privacy-safe (no PII).

may: Thanks team 44d I'll update the quickstart README and drop the harness script into the ticket.

sam: Will follow up here after staging runs.
